title: Dynamical magnetism in the disordered cubic lattice material $γ\text{−}{\mathrm{Ba}}_{3}{\mathrm{CoNb}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{9}$
summary: Strong disorder normally favors spin-glass freezing. Here, in contrast, the authors report an unconventional, highly fluctuating spin state in cubic γ-Ba CoNb O with effective spin-½ moments randomly diluted to just above the percolation limit. Neutron and muon measurements, with partially overlapping time windows, surprisingly reveal persistent correlated spin fluctuations from picoseconds to microseconds—a behavior reminiscent of quantum spin liquids. Numerical calculations suggest singlet formation is important. These results show disorder can sustain dynamic spin correlations even without strong geometrical frustration.
